newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian tax code to cut many tax privileges.
newsitem.headline: New Russian tax code to cut many tax privileges.

text.p: A new Russian tax code under government consideration will eliminate many tax privileges, simplify tax laws and cut the number of taxes, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Tuesday.
"The current tax system is exhausted," Livshits told a news conference. "It cannot fulfill the goals of the current stage of economic development."
He said he expected the code to be adopted this year so that it could come into force on January 1, 1998.
The State Duma lower house of parliament is reviewing the first part of the code outlining tax definitions and objectives.
The Constitutional Court is reviewing parts two, three and four before they are passed on to the Duma, Livshits said.
The value of Russian tax privileges in 1996 amounted to 175 trillion roubles, he said, adding the finance ministry had cut privileges by 70 trillion roubles in the draft tax code.
"We are categorically against these privileges: they are ineffective, unjust, unsystematic and we must put an end to them," he said.

Livshits said the draft code provided for cutting profit tax by two percentage points from the current 35 percent and a finance ministry statement said the code would eliminate a variable rate sales tax.
Livshits said the new code would include a list of permissible taxes and tax rates which the federal and local governments could impose.
Currently there are no restrictions on regional administrations' rights to levy taxes.
Investors in Russia often complain that taxes are too high and change too often.
Livshits said the Finance Ministry insisted that the new tax code not be changed within the next few years.
Poor tax revenues prompted the International Monetary Fund to temporarily withhold two tranches of its $10 billion loan to Russia late last year.
But official figures show that tax arrears rose to 128.25 trillion roubles at the start of this year, more than twice the level at the start of 1996.
